tagline: Downhill through the hemlocks to a road built for a waterfall.
intro: From US 64 at Sapphire, NC 281 heads south and down, curving through dense forest past Gorges State Park to the South Carolina line, where it turns into SC 130. It is 8.7 miles. This stretch was laid out in 1980, chiefly to bring visitors to the Whitewater Falls overlook.

Large stands of hemlock and spruce line the way, and in spring native azaleas, rhododendron and mountain laurel bloom beneath them. In 1916 the dam holding Lake Toxaway broke, and the flood down the Toxaway River scoured the gorges the state park now holds, leaving debris piled 15 to 20 feet high.

moments.title: Gorges State Park
moments.text: The Grassy Ridge entrance off NC 281 leads to Rainbow and Turtleback falls on the Horsepasture River, in a park that gets over 91 inches of rain a year.

moments.title: Upper Whitewater Falls
moments.text: A short walk from the road, the Whitewater River drops off the mountains close to the South Carolina border, seen from platforms set at several heights.

practical: The road is not recommended for recreational vehicles or buses, and the state guidebook notes that tractor-trailers are prohibited.

sources.label: NCDOT, North Carolina Scenic Byways guidebook, Whitewater Way
